subject: HERA pilot: dedicated slab recommendation & surge playbook
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@hera.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot sizing ask — expected bursts and latency SLO

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering lead asked for a concrete proposal on Dedicated capacity for the pilot so we can size procurement and get an internal cost sign-off. A few details on our side:

- Peak request pattern: 1–2 minute bursts, approx 750 concurrent user sessions during a campaign window.
- Average prompt length is ~120 tokens, responses average ~220 tokens. So typical request ~340 tokens round-trip.
- Target latency SLO: 95th <= 450ms for top-1 generation (we understand this is tight).
- Expected pilot duration: 6 weeks; daily active windows are 10:00–14:00 PT and 18:00–22:00 PT.

Can you put together tokens/sec estimates, recommended slab (GPU pool), and headroom guidance (safety buffer for campaign spikes)? Also any notes on fallback variants if we exceed slab capacity mid-campaign.

Appreciate a ballpark by EOD so I can brief procurement.

Cheers,
Elena
Elena Park
Director of Product
Hera Health
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@hera.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask — expected bursts and latency SLO

Elena — thanks for the clear traffic signal. I ran a quick preliminary calc with Marissa (cc'd) and attached a headroom spreadsheet. High level findings:

- Baseline tokens/sec estimate: with 750 concurrent sessions * 340 tokens = 255k tokens per second if all requests are truly simultaneous. However, realistic model concurrency (server-side) is lower because sessions start/complete over seconds, so we model an effective concurrency factor of ~0.25–0.4 for campaign bursts. That yields 64k–102k tokens/sec sustained during the peak window.
- Latency SLO fit: to hit 95th <= 450ms we recommend a ded. slab that gives single-request p99 ~ 350–380ms headroom (with autoscale headroom margin turned on). This points to a 4-GPU slab of A100-equivalent capacity for the pilot's expected pattern, with burst credits and an elastic overflow policy.
- Headroom: we propose a 30–40% safety buffer above modeled sustained tokens/sec to cover microbursts and slightly heavier prompts.

Attachments: hera_headroom_calc.xlsx — contains the token-per-second scenarios, per-GPU TPS assumptions, and latency budget math.

Marissa — can you weigh in on quantization/latency tweaks and whether a 3-GPU slab with aggressive batching could plausibly meet the SLO? Also note on fallback model variants (smaller model, 2-stage scoring) would be helpful.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask — Pilot sizing ask — notes from SE on latency assumptions

Looping Priyom for capacity modeling. Quick SE notes (assumptions are in the spreadsheet tabs):

- Model variant: we benchmarked the candidate open model (redwood-legacy-7b-qa) at 360 tokens/sec per A100 when running 16 concurrent streams with 32-token generation per step in our internal microbenchmarks. Those numbers scale non-linearly with sequence length so I adjusted for your 340-token average.
- Effective per-GPU TPS: after accounting for KV cache behavior and prefix overlaps, we used 22k–28k tokens/sec per GPU as the practical range for your workload.
- Batching: continuous batching helps throughput but can hurt P95. For your 95th <= 450ms target, we keep batch windows small (max 10ms) and rely on the dedicated slab to avoid queuing.
- Fallbacks: recommend an overflow policy that routes to a lower-cost model (redwood-3b-fast) for non-critical requests and returns a graceful degradation notice when routed. Also propose a cached-response layer for repeated prompts in campaign windows.

If we assume 25k tokens/sec per GPU, to cover the modeled 102k sustained peak we need ~4.1 GPUs => round to 5 GPUs for ops safety. With 35% headroom we get to ~6.8 => recommend committing to a 6-GPU slab for the pilot, with an option to scale to 8 for full campaigns.

Priyom — can you run the slab-cost delta (3 vs 4 vs 6 GPUs) and note lead time to spin up additional capacity in Dedicated?

—Marissa
(se)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procure@hera.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask — dedicated slab recommendation & surge playbook

Elena — quick summary & recommendation after internal sizing: please see the attached SLA draft and headroom workbook. TL;DR:

Recommendation (pilot): commit to a 6-GPU Dedicated slab (A100-equivalent). Rationale: modeled sustained peak ~102k tokens/sec; at ~25k tokens/sec/GPU we need 4.1 GPUs; ops safety + 35% headroom => 6 GPUs. This meets 95th <= 450ms under our conservative latency assumptions when batching windows are constrained to 8–12ms.

Operational notes:
- Burst handling: enable burst credits + overlay an overflow routing policy to route excess traffic to a pre-authorized lower-cost model (redwood-3b-fast) with a throughput cap.
- Fallback behavior: non-interactive or low-priority requests should be routed to the fallback model; interactive sessions get priority queuing.
- Observability: we'll add per-route token counters and a rolling 60s TPS gauge to your Console project; alerts at 70% and 90% slab utilization.
- Procurement note: procurement should expect a start-of-pilot commit for 6 GPUs with optional add-on for +2 GPUs for campaign spikes. Lead time to add GPUs to Dedicated: nominally 24–48 hours for capacity in our US region, expedited by a short-term burst in hosted pools if needed.

Attached: HERA_SLA_draft_v1.docx (SLA + rollback/fallback clauses), hera_headroom_calc.xlsx (detailed math). HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/5963/DEAL-2027-0421.

Next steps: if procurement approves the 6-GPU pilot, we'll issue a draft commitment and schedule an onboarding call with Solutions + Infra to lock the routing policy and alert thresholds.

Ben
